settings_automation_invalid: Line under an automation in the crewmate's settings when hostd's cron parser refuses its schedule (saved under an older parser): it is kept as saved and never runs until it is fixed or deleted. {reason} is the parser's own message, English, shown as is.
settings_display_language_description: Help line under the Display language row in Settings > General. Says what the setting changes; the picker's first option explains what following the system means.
settings_display_language_env_override: Notice under the Display language row when the ATLAS_LANG environment variable forces a language, so a saved choice has no visible effect. Keep ATLAS_LANG untranslated.
settings_display_language_failed: Error toast when saving the language fails. {error} is a technical reason from the app, usually English.
settings_display_language_label: Name of the Settings row that picks the language of the app interface. NOT the Languages tab, which is about programming languages.
settings_display_language_match_system: First option of the Display language picker while a language is saved: use the operating system's language instead of a fixed one.
settings_display_language_match_system_w: First option of the Display language picker while the app follows the system. {language} is the language that results, written in its own name (English, Português), so the user sees what Match system means right now.
settings_group_language: Title of the card in Settings > General that holds the Display language row. Also shown as the group name in settings search results.
settings_host_action_dont_wait: Ghost button on the Terminal host tile while a restart waits for the terminals to go idle; cancels the wait.
settings_host_action_restart: Button on the Terminal host tile that restarts the host right away, because no terminal is running.

settings_host_action_restart_confirm.description: Button on the Terminal host tile that opens a confirmation first, because running terminals would end. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
settings_host_action_restart_confirm.distinct: opens a confirmation dialog first, hence the ellipsis

settings_host_badge_postponed: Small badge on the Terminal host tile: the user chose to restart later this session.
settings_host_badge_restarts_when_idle: Small badge on the Terminal host tile: the host will restart by itself once no terminal is busy.
settings_host_name: Name of the tile in Settings > General for the background process that runs the terminals (hostd). Keep host.
settings_host_sub_current: One line under the Terminal host tile name when the host is current. {count} is the number of running terminals; zero reads as none.
settings_host_sub_older: One line under the Terminal host tile name when the host is older than the app. {version} is the Atlas version, {count} the number of running terminals; zero reads as none.
settings_host_sub_restarting: Status on the Terminal host tile while the host restarts.
settings_host_sub_updating: Status on the Terminal host tile during a live upgrade of the host: the terminals keep running.
settings_updates_withdrawn_older: Sentence in the withdrawn-version warning when the newest safe release is OLDER than the installed one, so the install button at the bottom of the page rolls back.
settings_updates_withdrawn_replacement: Sentence in the withdrawn-version warning naming the release that replaces it. {replacement} is a version such as v1.5.0, shown as is.
settings_updates_withdrawn_title: Title of the warning in Settings > Updates when the installed version is on the withdrawn (yanked) list. The reason the maintainers wrote follows as the body.
settings_updates_withdrawn_update: Sentence in the withdrawn-version warning when a newer safe release is offered: updating gets the user off the withdrawn one.
